organisation.name: Vault (the service organisation)
organisation.scope: The Vault platform: ingestion, the gate, the fact store, the sealed archive, the ledger, and the control surface.

observationWindow.minimumPeriod: 3 months for an initial Type II; 6 or 12 months is what most enterprise buyers accept
observationWindow.statement: 47 of 51 controls can only be evidenced over an observation period. Until that period has elapsed and been audited, this is a Type I position — a point-in-time design assessment — however complete the control matrix looks.

controls.name: Demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values
controls.how: Board-level policy and a code of conduct. Organisational, not technical.
controls.gap: Requires a signed code of conduct and evidence of annual acknowledgement. No software artefact satisfies this.

controls.name: Board exercises oversight responsibility
controls.how: The board reporting pack is generated from the live register and the ledger.

evidence.what: The AI system inventory, as a stream of registration events with named owners.

controls.gap: Needs minuted board meetings across the observation window.

controls.name: Management establishes structure, authority and responsibility
controls.how: Every agent, folder and namespace carries a named business owner and technical owner, enforced at registration.

evidence.what: The AI system inventory, as a stream of registration events with named owners.

controls.name: Demonstrates commitment to competence
controls.how: HR process: role descriptions, hiring criteria, training records.
controls.gap: Requires training records over the observation window.

controls.name: Enforces accountability
controls.how: Every review decision and admin action is attributed to a named actor in the tamper-evident ledger.

evidence.what: Human review decisions with actor, timing and reasoning.
Chain anchoring and export events; the chain itself is the evidence.

controls.name: Obtains or generates relevant quality information
controls.how: The ledger is the information system: every gate verdict, review decision and admin action, hash-chained.

evidence.what: Human review decisions with actor, timing and reasoning.
Chain anchoring and export events; the chain itself is the evidence.

controls.name: Internally communicates information
controls.how: Alerts route to the named folder owner with severity tiering and delivery across six channels.

evidence.what: Human review decisions with actor, timing and reasoning.

controls.name: Communicates with external parties
controls.how: Erasure receipts, DSAR responses, breach notification timelines and the published status page.

evidence.what: Erasure executions with their receipts and the keys destroyed.

controls.name: Specifies objectives with sufficient clarity
controls.how: Documented in the system description and the risk register.

controls.name: Identifies and analyses risk
controls.how: The risk register, plus adversarial testing of the gate itself.

evidence.what: Adversarial findings and detector firings.

controls.name: Considers the potential for fraud
controls.justification: Directly applicable: the product exists to resist deliberate manipulation.
controls.how: Channel trust, wall enforcement, and the poisoning detectors — the threat model is an adversary writing to memory.

evidence.what: Writes refused or held on channel-trust grounds.
Wall configuration changes and every privileged access grant.

controls.name: Identifies and analyses significant change
controls.how: Model-pin change detection, rule version control, framework-change tracking.

evidence.what: Model pins recorded at registration and every change to them.

controls.name: Selects, develops and performs ongoing evaluations
controls.how: Continuous control monitoring, plus quarterly red-teaming of the gate.

evidence.what: Adversarial findings and detector firings.

controls.name: Evaluates and communicates deficiencies
controls.how: The incident register with classification, root cause, remediation and disclosure tracking.

evidence.what: Adversarial findings and detector firings.

controls.name: Selects and develops control activities
controls.how: The ten-check gate, which cannot be disabled in any configuration.

evidence.what: Gate verdicts. Every write carries the outcome of all ten checks.

controls.name: Selects and develops general technology controls
controls.how: Gate, ledger, encryption at rest, key management.

evidence.what: Gate verdicts. Every write carries the outcome of all ten checks.
Chain anchoring and export events; the chain itself is the evidence.

controls.name: Deploys through policies and procedures
controls.how: Published policies with versioning, approval and acknowledgement tracking.

controls.name: Implements logical access security
controls.how: SAML/OIDC SSO, server-side sessions, MFA with phishing-resistant factors for privileged roles, RBAC and ABAC, folder walls.

evidence.what: Gate verdicts. Every write carries the outcome of all ten checks.
Wall configuration changes and every privileged access grant.

controls.name: Registers and authorises new users
controls.how: SCIM provisioning from the customer IdP; agents require named owners at registration.

evidence.what: The AI system inventory, as a stream of registration events with named owners.

controls.name: Removes access when no longer required
controls.how: SCIM deprovisioning revokes server-side sessions on the NEXT request; measured worst case 7.69ms across 12 routes.

evidence.what: Wall configuration changes and every privileged access grant.

controls.name: Restricts physical access
controls.justification: Included for Vault Cloud, inherited from the IaaS provider under a carve-out or inclusive method.
controls.how: Inherited from the cloud provider; out of scope for on-prem deployments where the customer controls the facility.
controls.gap: Requires the sub-service organisation report (AWS/Azure/GCP SOC 2) and a decision on carve-out vs inclusive.

controls.name: Disposes of data securely
controls.how: Receipted erasure: hard delete with segment rewrite, plus crypto-shredding that reaches backup generations.

evidence.what: Erasure executions with their receipts and the keys destroyed.

controls.name: Restricts access from outside the system boundary
controls.how: TLS 1.3, mTLS for agent connections, IP allowlisting, geo-fencing, device binding.

evidence.what: Gate verdicts. Every write carries the outcome of all ten checks.

controls.name: Restricts transmission and movement of information
controls.how: PII detection and masking at ingestion, wall enforcement on exports, residency pinning with cross-border read blocking.

evidence.what: Wall configuration changes and every privileged access grant.

controls.name: Prevents or detects unauthorised software
controls.how: Tool and MCP server allowlisting with provenance; approved-model allowlist.

evidence.what: Tool and MCP allowlisting decisions.

controls.name: Detects and monitors configuration changes
controls.how: Every rule change, wall change, module toggle and model pin change is a ledger event.

evidence.what: Chain anchoring and export events; the chain itself is the evidence.
Model pins recorded at registration and every change to them.

controls.name: Monitors for anomalies and security events
controls.how: Fourteen poisoning detectors, per-agent behavioural baselines with deviation alerting, SIEM export.

evidence.what: Chain anchoring and export events; the chain itself is the evidence.
Adversarial findings and detector firings.

controls.name: Evaluates security events for impact
controls.how: Contagion trace: origin, read-by list, derived facts, affected summaries, blast-radius summary.

evidence.what: Chain anchoring and export events; the chain itself is the evidence.

controls.name: Responds to identified security incidents
controls.how: Documented incident response plan; six-level kill switch with a named administrator.

evidence.what: Kill switch activations, including scheduled tests.

controls.name: Recovers from identified security incidents
controls.how: Point-in-time restore, one-click rollback of a fact/agent/source/channel/folder, incident bundle export.

evidence.what: Kill switch activations, including scheduled tests.

controls.name: Authorises, designs, develops, tests and approves changes
controls.how: Rule lifecycle draft → backtest → warn-only → enforce, with version control and a named approver.

evidence.what: Model pins recorded at registration and every change to them.

controls.gap: Requires evidence of code review and CI gating across the observation window; no CI configuration is currently committed.

controls.name: Identifies and mitigates business disruption risk
controls.how: Backup and DR with measured RPO/RTO, continuous mirror export to customer-owned storage, self-host escape hatch.

evidence.what: Kill switch activations, including scheduled tests.

controls.name: Assesses and manages vendor and business partner risk
controls.how: Third-party AI vendor register with sub-processor, attestation and renewal-date tracking.

evidence.what: Vendor register entries and attestation tracking.

controls.name: Maintains and monitors capacity
controls.justification: Selected. Customers contract to an availability SLA, so capacity monitoring is in scope.
controls.how: Live cost/GB per tier, growth forecasting, hard caps with pre-breach alerts, storage chargeback.

controls.name: Environmental protections, backup and recovery infrastructure
controls.justification: Selected. Backup and recovery infrastructure is the mechanism behind the availability commitment; without it the SLA is unbacked.
controls.how: Continuous incremental plus daily full, cross-region replication, immutable backups with separate delete credentials.

evidence.what: Kill switch activations, including scheduled tests.

controls.name: Tests recovery plan procedures
controls.justification: Selected. A recovery plan that has never been executed is a document; the drill is what makes the commitment real.
controls.how: Quarterly restore drill spawning a fresh Vault from the export alone; DR exercise with the primary genuinely destroyed.

evidence.what: Kill switch activations, including scheduled tests.

controls.name: Identifies and maintains confidential information
controls.justification: Selected. The service holds customer confidential information by design, so confidentiality is a criterion the buyer relies on.
controls.how: Four-tier sensitivity labelling with folder inheritance and never-guess-downward.
controls.gap: Mapped to a Vault control, but no ledger entry has been produced yet. Exercise the control, or confirm it is not reachable in this deployment.

controls.name: Disposes of confidential information
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Receipted erasure with crypto-shredding; retention schedules with conflict surfacing.

evidence.what: Erasure executions with their receipts and the keys destroyed.

controls.name: Obtains or generates relevant quality information about objectives
controls.justification: Selected. The service asserts that stored memory is traceable to its source, which is a processing-integrity claim.
controls.how: Provenance on every fact: source span, channel, trust classification, model version, extraction confidence.

evidence.what: Chain anchoring and export events; the chain itself is the evidence.

controls.name: Inputs are complete and accurate
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Ten-check gate; conservative extraction that holds rather than invents; never-invent rule with every candidate traceable to a byte range.

evidence.what: Gate verdicts. Every write carries the outcome of all ten checks.
Writes refused or held on channel-trust grounds.

controls.name: Processing is complete, accurate and timely
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Measured gate latency; queue-and-drain fail-safe with no pass-unchecked path.

evidence.what: Gate verdicts. Every write carries the outcome of all ten checks.

controls.name: Outputs are complete, accurate and distributed appropriately
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Read path filters by wall, clearance, region and status, and labels every returned fact with provenance.

evidence.what: Wall configuration changes and every privileged access grant.

controls.name: Stores inputs and outputs completely and accurately
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: WORM raw archive, hash-chained, with retention schedules.

evidence.what: Chain anchoring and export events; the chain itself is the evidence.
Retention executions and legal holds.

controls.name: Notice about privacy practices
controls.justification: Selected. The service processes personal data on behalf of customers as a processor under GDPR Article 28.
controls.how: Auto-generated employee transparency notice; jurisdiction packs ship a plain-language scope statement.
controls.gap: Mapped to a Vault control, but no ledger entry has been produced yet. Exercise the control, or confirm it is not reachable in this deployment.

controls.name: Choice and consent
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Lawful basis per fact, Art 9 conditions, DPDP Consent Manager integration, withdrawal triggering real purge.

evidence.what: Lawful basis records and withdrawals.

controls.name: Collection limited to identified purposes
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: PII controls at ingestion; Employee Privacy Mode excluded contexts; sample-not-stream default.
controls.gap: Mapped to a Vault control, but no ledger entry has been produced yet. Exercise the control, or confirm it is not reachable in this deployment.

controls.name: Use, retention and disposal
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Purpose limitation enforced at read time; retention by purpose alongside retention by age.

evidence.what: Retention executions and legal holds.
Erasure executions with their receipts and the keys destroyed.

controls.name: Access by data subjects
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: DSAR workflow with full-person discovery, machine-readable output, third-party redaction, deadline tracking.

evidence.what: Erasure executions with their receipts and the keys destroyed.

controls.name: Disclosure to third parties
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Sub-processor list per region; third-party erasure propagation with confirmation.

evidence.what: Vendor register entries and attestation tracking.

controls.name: Quality of personal information
controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Rectification workflow with versioning; contradiction resolution with human arbitration.

evidence.what: Erasure executions with their receipts and the keys destroyed.

controls.justification: Selected. In scope because the service commits to this criterion contractually and the buyer relies on it.
controls.how: Employee objection channel with tracked response; works-council role; change notification to representatives.
